label: sparse copy-phase update-gate unit, favours fed-back g/r/o/2/t/3/c/y (no clean rule)
explanation: Active only in the copy phase, never during original input or at the delimiter, never on the first copy output (recall_idx 0), and only when 5 or fewer outputs remain. It fires only when the fed-back input is a repeat (in_first=0, which always holds in the copy phase). Even inside that window the rate is just ~2.6%. Rates are highest at L=3 (11%) and at the final steps of L=9, and for fed-back inputs g, r, o, 2, t, 3, c, y (2-5x lift) and outputs c, y, 0, 2. Restricting to those inputs covers ~80% of activation mass but precision is only ~8%, and adding an output-token set gives at best F1 ~0.22. Activation depends on some token/position combination that simple per-step or history variables do not capture. Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.005) and the top examples are mostly the last step of L=3 sequences or early copy steps of L=9 sequences.
